sections.html:
Auburn is the seat of Androscoggin County and sits on the Androscoggin River directly across from Lewiston. The two are called the Twin Cities, or Lewiston-Auburn, and share one metro area. About 24,000 people lived here at the 2020 census.

The city is big for its population, at 65.74 square miles, of which 59.33 are land. Over the years it took in land from Poland, Minot and the whole town of Danville, so a compact river downtown sits alongside farmland, lake property and rural roads. Lake Auburn supplies public water for the area.

That spread matters when you sell, because the rules change by neighborhood. A downtown house on public sewer faces one set of requirements, and a lake-area house on a septic system faces another, as the septic section below explains.

Much of the older housing dates from the shoe-factory boom, when the population grew from about 4,000 in 1860 to 12,000 by 1890. A house that old can have original wiring, an aging roof or a foundation that needs work. Those are the items a conventional buyer's inspector tends to list, and they are common reasons an owner looks for an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What does an Auburn property tax bill look like?
sections.html:
For the 2026-27 fiscal year, Auburn's rate is $24.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, and real estate bills are paid in two installments, one in September and one in March. The next installment is due March 15, 2027, with interest starting March 16.

Fiscal year 2026-27 tax figures
Tax detailFiscal year 2026-27
Tax rate$24.50 per $1,000 of assessment
State certified ratio73 percent
Second installment dueMarch 15, 2027 (interest begins March 16)
Homestead exemption$18,250 off assessment, worth $447.13 in tax

After a sale, send the bill on to your mortgage holder or to the new owner, and tell the tax office who now owns the house. Because the March installment falls in spring, a spring sale usually needs a payoff or a proration of that bill.

Applications for the homestead, blind and veteran exemptions are due by April 1 for the following tax year. A buyer who wants the homestead exemption has to file their own application, since yours does not follow the house.

If you think your assessment is too high, Maine law requires a written request to the assessor within 185 days of the date the value was committed to the tax collector. The city explains the process on its abatements page. Auburn's assessing division also runs a citywide revaluation hub, so values may be reset in the coming years, and a buyer may ask what your new number will be.

sections.h2: Does Auburn require a septic inspection when you sell?
sections.html:
Yes, for homes in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District that are not on public sewer. An inspection report has to be provided to the city when such a property is sold.

  • The rule covers owners in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District whose buildings are not served by public sewer.
  • A certified subsurface wastewater system inspector must do the work, using minimum requirements set by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services.
  • The owner arranges and pays for the inspection, and costs vary by inspector.
  • Reports go to the city's Planning, Permitting and Code Department by email, paper or the SmartGov portal.
  • If the report shows a failed system, the local plumbing inspector reviews it, and a failed system has to be replaced with a new one.

The septic program began in spring 2025 under an ordinance effective July 15, 2024, and it cycles through five years of designated areas. A lake-area seller should check the city's map early, because a failed system turns a fast sale into a repair project.

A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take on that risk, but the inspection report still has to be filed. Ask any buyer, including us, how the septic requirement will be handled at the closing table.

sections.h2: Flood, watershed and vacant building rules
sections.html:
Two more city rules come up often: flood hazard permits and vacant building registration. The Planning, Permitting and Code Department administers both.

  • Flood hazard areas. FEMA's revised floodplain maps for Androscoggin County were adopted on July 8, 2013. Development in a special flood hazard area, including placing a manufactured home, needs a flood hazard development permit on top of any other permits. Check the FEMA map for your address before listing.
  • Taylor Pond and Lake Auburn overlays. Both watershed overlay districts carry extra zoning rules meant to protect water quality.
  • Vacant buildings. The owner of a vacant or abandoned building has to apply for a vacant building registration permit, and the permit is posted by the primary entrance. A fee schedule applies, with an added fee for buildings designated high impact. If you inherited an empty house, ask the code office whether it has to be registered.

None of these rules stops a sale. They do shape what a buyer's lender or inspector will ask for, which is why an as-is buyer can often close faster than a financed one.

sections.h2: Fees and taxes when you sell
sections.html:
As the seller you owe half of Maine's real estate transfer tax, plus any mortgage payoff, unpaid property tax and the cost of recording documents. The tax is $2.20 for every $500 of value, divided evenly between the two sides. Our Maine transfer tax guide covers the exemptions for inherited and divorce transfers.

Deeds in Auburn are recorded at the Androscoggin County Registry of Deeds, 2 Turner Street, Unit 4 (207-753-2500, extension 1981). The base fee is $35 by statute, and most Maine registries add a $5 surcharge. Our Maine deed recording guide has the details.

Property tax runs in two installments, so the current period is normally split between buyer and seller at closing.

sections.h2: Should you list, sell yourself or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
Listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and takes the longest. It also means preparing the house, since financed buyers usually order inspections. Selling it yourself saves the commission but puts the marketing, paperwork and negotiating on you. A cash offer is a purchase with no financing contingency, typically as-is, and the closing date is flexible.

We quote no price in advance and promise no amount. We look at the condition, location and what a house would sell for, and give you an offer you are free to turn down. Cash offers are often lower than a fully repaired retail listing, so compare the net you would receive, including repairs, carrying costs and commission, against the offer.

Cash offers fit best when the house needs work, when it was inherited, when tenants are in place, when a septic or title issue is pending, or when you need to close by a certain date.

Before you talk to any buyer, gather the deed, your mortgage payoff, the latest tax bill and, for a lake-area home, the status of your septic inspection.

faqs.q: How do I sell my house fast in Auburn, ME?
faqs.a: The fastest route is usually a cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is and does not need a mortgage. Listing with an agent is slower because buyers order inspections and appraisals. Either way, find out early whether your property needs a septic inspection report.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Auburn, Maine?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2026-27 the rate is $24.50 per $1,000 of assessed value. The second real estate installment is due March 15, 2027.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic inspection to sell in Auburn?
faqs.a: If the home is in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District and is not served by public sewer, the city requires an inspection report when the property is sold. Homes on public sewer or outside the district are not covered by that rule.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded in Auburn?
faqs.a: At the Androscoggin County Registry of Deeds at 2 Turner Street, Unit 4, Auburn. Call 207-753-2500, extension 1981, to confirm fees and recording hours before you submit anything.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Auburn?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the estate has the authority to sell, the house can be sold like any other. The deed that moves it from the estate to the heirs is exempt from transfer tax, but a later sale to a buyer is taxed, with the tax split evenly between buyer and seller.
